THE SKILL TREE

Calisthenics,
from zero.

Bodyweight strength is a skill. Build control first; harder variations can wait. Mark a step as familiar when it feels comfortable and controlled — not because you forced it.

01 · PUSH

Push-up pathway

Learn to keep your body steady and your shoulders comfortable.

Start: Wall push-ups · 3–6 controlled reps
Next: Higher-surface incline push-ups → lower incline → knee push-ups → floor push-ups
02 · LEGS

Squat & single-leg control

Use a comfortable range. A chair can be a target, not a test.

Start: Sit-to-stand from a sturdy chair · 4–8 reps
Next: Free squat → supported split squat → reverse lunge
03 · CORE

Core control

Slow, steady reps beat holding your breath or straining.

Start: Dead bug heel taps · 4–6 each side
Next: Dead bug extensions → short plank → longer plank
04 · PULL

Back & pull-up foundations

Pulling strength usually needs safe equipment. Don't hang from doors, towel racks or furniture that could tip.

Start: Shoulder-blade squeezes and controlled prone “W” raises
Next: Resistance-band rows or rows on a properly installed, rated bar → assisted hangs → assisted pull-ups
Progression rule: when you can do the top end of the reps smoothly, with no pain and a couple of reps still in reserve, try a slightly harder version next time. There is no deadline.

A gentle reminder

Food is training support. If you've barely eaten, feel shaky, or feel overheated, eat/drink and recover rather than forcing a session. With your history of being very underweight, focus on getting stronger and eating enough — not on getting leaner.
